name: Restrictive Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Evidence of impaired ventricular filling with restrictive physiology on echocardiography or cardiac catheterization
Preserved or near-normal left ventricular systolic function
Endomyocardial biopsy showing myocardial fibrosis or infiltration causing stiffness
Exclusion of other causes of restrictive physiology such as constrictive pericarditis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of impaired ventricular filling with restrictive physiology and preserved systolic function, excluding other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multimodal imaging and sometimes biopsy to confirm etiology

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated jugular venous pressure with prominent y descent

pathognomonic.notes: Paradoxical rise in jugular venous pressure on inspiration

common.notes: Due to elevated filling pressures and pulmonary congestion

occasional.notes: Secondary to low cardiac output or arrhythmias

rare.notes: Due to atrial enlargement and stasis

laboratory: Possible abnormal serum protein electrophoresis if amyloidosis present
imaging: Echocardiogram showing biatrial enlargement with normal ventricular size and preserved systolic function
Cardiac MRI showing myocardial fibrosis or infiltration
Endomyocardial biopsy confirming fibrosis or infiltration
genetic: Mutations in sarcomeric protein genes (e.g., TNNI3, TNNT2) in familial cases
Genetic testing for amyloidosis-related mutations (e.g., TTR gene)
other: Electrocardiogram may show low voltage or atrial enlargement
Right heart catheterization demonstrating elevated filling pressures with normal cardiac output

distinguishingFeatures: Pericardial thickening or calcification on imaging
History of pericardial disease or surgery
Systolic anterior motion of mitral valve
Dilated ventricular chambers with reduced systolic function

redFlags: Rapid progression of heart failure symptoms
Evidence of systemic amyloidosis or infiltrative disease
references: Maron BJ, Towbin JA, Thiene G, et al. Contemporary definitions and classification of the cardiomyopathies: an American Heart Association Scientific Statement. Circulation. 2006;113(14):1807-1816.

Elliott P, Andersson B, Arbustini E, et al. Classification of the cardiomyopathies: a position statement from the European Society Of Cardiology Working Group on Myocardial and Pericardial Diseases. Eur Heart J. 2008;29(2):270-276.
Muchtar E, Blauwet LA, Gertz MA. Restrictive Cardiomyopathy: Genetics, Pathogenesis, Clinical Manifestations, Diagnosis, and Therapy. Circ Res. 2017;121(7):819-837.
